complexity.notes: The set holds node objects, whose hashes come from CPython's identity hash (allocator-chosen addresses), so lookups are O(1) worst case with no adversarial-collision concern. The variable i is incremented every iteration but never read — dead code that can be dropped. A better approach exists that keeps the same O(n) time but reduces space to O(1): ||Floyd's tortoise-and-hare: advance two pointers at speeds 1 and 2; they meet inside a cycle iff one exists||.
complexity.summary: Walks the list one node at a time, storing each visited node object in a set and returning True the moment a node is seen twice; returns False if the walk reaches None.
